steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
/app/bin/pitchurn sits on this image. Source fixes under /app are required for the Java mill pipeline directories listed in `/app/deskfold/ROUTE.txt`. A static or hand-written tally is not enough; rebuild the mill from those units, then anneal, and leave it that way. Verifier reruns the mill verbs listed in `/app/deskfold/BUILD.txt`. Notes live under /app/deskfold. Card layout lives in `/app/deskfold/CARD.txt`.

Ops tightened `/app/gearpit/live.gear` hoping never-seen intake would land as smaller unique pieces. anneal prints walked. A second stow of `/app/filmwelle/stable.bin` exits 0 and draw of that reel writes the same bytes as the file, yet reuse_frac on that pass sits near 0.00 and bytes_stored tracks bytes_in. The same restow contract applies to /app/filmwelle/plain.bin and /app/filmwelle/brine.bin. Mean piece length on a reel the mill has never seen stays in the old band.

/app/urnbay/tally.json follows the card file above. Named card entries are reel, bytes_in, bytes_stored, reuse_frac, mean_piece, and piece_count; numeric entries are base-10 strings. reel is the basename of the stowed path. Re-stowing a reel whose bytes already sit in the silo keeps reuse_frac at or above 0.80. Mean piece length for a never-seen reel is at or below 2048. A stow that writes a full new copy of already-siloed bytes exits non-zero. draw DEST writes the same bytes as the source reel.

steps.message:
Analysis: The routed Java source directories are oxemit, nincut, coldrib, and hitchcli. The live chunking mask is 2047, but observed behavior suggests either chunk boundary logic or index reuse is defective. Existing silo data and idx.tsv are present, while tally.json is absent. We must understand the prescribed CLI syntax, generated classes, index format, and notes before patching.
Plan: Read all notes, build/launcher scripts, and every routed Java source file. Also inspect the seed/current indexes and compare live versus legacy gear settings. This will reveal how chunk generation, stow reuse, annealing, tally output, and exit codes work.

steps.message:
Analysis: The notes identify the intended migration issue: older silo pieces were made with legacy gear, while live gear now creates smaller chunks. Simply annealing under live gear appears to have appended another incompatible index view, explaining the doubled current idx.tsv and near-zero reuse. We need inspect the complete generated span logic and CLI classes because the prior combined output was truncated.
Plan: Print the generator and hitchcli files individually with line numbers, plus all index/manifest formats and CLI usage behavior. Then we can patch anneal/index handling so existing large blobs are rechunked or otherwise indexed compatibly under live gear, while preserving exact draw manifests and enforcing duplicate-restow failure.

/app/bin/pitchurn 2>&1 || true; /app/bin/pitchurn census 2>&1; echo census_rc=$?; /app/bin/pitchurn stow 2>&1 || echo stow_rc=$?; /app/bin/pitchurn draw 2>&1 || echo draw_rc=$?

steps.message:
Analysis: Anneal is definitively broken: generated Span.merge merely appends hot/idx.tsv to idx.tsv on every run, causing duplicate growth and doing nothing to make legacy large pieces reusable under live chunking. Census currently exits 1, likely because tally state is missing. The full StowRun/CardRun details were still truncated and are essential before implementing the migration.
Plan: Fetch each operational class in smaller separate outputs and inspect the current tally-related files. Also calculate counts and duplicates per index. With those details, patch the generator-backed anneal implementation and any stow/card logic necessary for accurate dynamic metrics and duplicate-copy rejection.

arguments.keystrokes: find /app/urnbay/marks -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f %s\n' -exec sh -c 'echo --- $1; cat "$1"' sh {} \; | head -250; echo '--- index stats ---'; for f in /app/urnbay/idx.tsv /app/urnbay/hot/idx.tsv /app/urnbay/keep/idx.tsv /app/urnbay/cold/idx.tsv; do printf '%s lines=' "$f"; wc -l < "$f"; printf ' unique='; cut -f1 "$f" | sort -u | wc -l; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The root cause is clear: anneal only concatenates hot/idx.tsv onto idx.tsv, repeatedly duplicating entries. It never reconstructs legacy-manifest reels and rechunks them with live.gear, so live stow cannot find its smaller chunks. The existing manifests and cold/keep/hot indexes provide everything needed to rebuild each reel exactly. Stow's tally is dynamically computed and its full-copy duplicate rejection already exists.
Plan: Replace WalkRun with a real, idempotent anneal: load all silo indexes including cold, reconstruct every marked reel in manifest order, rechunk bytes using live.gear, store only genuinely absent live chunks, append their index entries, and rewrite manifests to live chunk keys. It will print exactly 'walked'. Then rebuild with kiln, restore the seed snapshot to test from the verifier-like initial state, anneal, test all three restows and draws, inspect tallies and chunk means, test idempotent anneal, and leave the silo annealed.

arguments.keystrokes: rm -rf /app/urnbay; cp -a /app/seed/urnbay /app/urnbay; /app/bin/pitchurn anneal; echo anneal_rc=$?; wc -l /app/urnbay/idx.tsv; for r in stable.bin plain.bin brine.bin; do /app/bin/pitchurn stow "/app/filmwelle/$r"; rc=$?; echo "stow $r rc=$rc"; cat /app/urnbay/tally.json; /app/bin/pitchurn draw "/app/urnbay/$r.out" "/app/filmwelle/$r"; cmp "/app/filmwelle/$r" "/app/urnbay/$r.out" && echo "draw $r OK"; done

echo '--- second anneal idempotence ---'; before=$(wc -l < /app/urnbay/idx.tsv); /app/bin/pitchurn anneal; after=$(wc -l < /app/urnbay/idx.tsv); echo "idx_lines_before=$before idx_lines_after=$after"; /app/bin/pitchurn stow /app/filmwelle/stable.bin; echo restow_rc=$?; cat /app/urnbay/tally.json; /app/bin/pitchurn census; echo census_rc=$?; cat /app/urnbay/tally.json

steps.message:
Analysis: The mill has been fixed and rebuilt. Anneal now reconstructs marked reels from silo manifests, rechunks them under live.gear, indexes missing live chunks, rewrites manifests, detects missing keys/hash collisions, and is idempotent. From a restored seed snapshot, all three required reels restowed with reuse_frac 1.0000 and bytes_stored 0; their means were <=2048, draws matched byte-for-byte, census succeeded, and a second anneal left index size unchanged. We should only remove temporary draw outputs and run anneal once more so the final state is clean and explicitly annealed.
Plan: Delete the three test draw outputs, invoke the rebuilt mill's anneal verb one final time, and confirm the key state files remain present. This leaves the required rebuilt and annealed installation in place.
